text:
incident-bot: Paging sara (SRE - oncall): elevated 5xx rate and streaming disconnects observed across gateway -> backend fanout. Auto-escalation threshold hit. Impact: some streaming sessions disconnect mid-response, chunked encoding errors reported by clients.

sara (SRE - oncall): seeing it, joining. What dashboards look like?

mike (infra): HTTP 502/504 spike from gateway -> runtime, fanout RPS up ~1.8x on a few customers. Error rate ~4.6% overall, but streaming endpoints hit ~12% for certain routes.

kevin (runtime): getting a ton of partial-chunk, premature EOF logs from runtime proxies. Hypothesis: worker OOMs causing connection close during chunk stream assembly.

carla (eng): can you paste the logs?

kevin (runtime): here are last 10 lines from runtime proxy (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] conn=abcd1234 error=write: broken pipe chunked_writer.go:87
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] conn=abcd1234 worker-pid=421 SIGTERM oom-killer maybe
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] conn=efgh5678 upstream=10.2.4.12:5005 502 head-of-line timeout
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] conn=ijkl9012 client-cancel received
```

tess (support): three customers (A, B, C) reported reconnect loops and aborted responses. Customer A sees chunked decoder errors in their SDK.

sara (SRE - oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) reduce fanout concurrency for streaming requests, 2) route heavy customers to a fallback model that is single-shard, 3) raise gateway timeouts to avoid mid-chunk kills while we stabilize. I'm going to adjust route policies now.

mike (infra): adjusting fanout concurrency -> set MAX_FANOUT=8 for streaming workerpool via k8s configmap. Patching now:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/streaming-worker MAX_FANOUT=8 --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-worker
```

kevin (runtime): I'm pinning model variants for affected routes to the low-memory quantized variant and enabling aggressive KV-cache reuse. This should reduce memory churn.

carla (eng): can we also temporary throttling at gateway for requests with big context length? Those blow memory.

mike (infra): added nginx rate limit for header X-Client-Context-Length > 12000: limit_req zone=context burst=2 nodelay. Patch applied.

pagerduty-bot: sara acknowledged the page.

sara (SRE - oncall): rolling change looks good so far, error rate down from 12% -> 6% on streaming route in last 3 minutes. Client cancels still present but fewer 5xx.

kevin (runtime): still seeing intermittent chunked encoding truncation where generator hit worker restart. Collecting core dumps and uploading to staging S3: s3://redwood-ops/incident-4089990123/coredumps

carla (eng): any chance the kernel update from yesterday caused epoll regression? We saw that before.

mike (infra): can confirm one node profile shows a recent kernel patch; I've cordoned node ip-10-2-4-12 and booted a fresh node without patch. Traffic routed away from suspect node.

tess (support): customer A reports improvement but wants timeline.

sara (SRE - oncall): tell them we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA within 24h. No persistent data loss; some streaming sessions were aborted and clients should reconnect.

kevin (runtime): temporary mitigation summary I'm pushing to the team: reduced fanout concurrency, pinned to quantized variant, enabled KV-cache reuse, throttled long-context requests, cordoned suspect node.

carla (eng): any config we should revert once stable? We should not keep increased timeouts long-term.

mike (infra): agreed. Plan: monitor for 30m post-stable window, then roll back TIMEOUT change to baseline and gradually restore MAX_FANOUT.

sara (SRE - oncall): assigning follow-ups:
- kevin: collect and triage core dumps, correlate with oom logs (due EOD)
- mike: rebuild image for node with kernel patch, run soak tests (due +8h)
- carla: evaluate memory usage pattern and model variant impact (due +24h)
- tess: customer comms & impact spreadsheet (due +2h)

pagerduty-bot: escalation cleared by sara. No further paging.

sara (SRE - oncall): concise incident summary for handoff:
```
- Incident TS: 4089990123
- Symptom: elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects (chunked truncation / client cancels)
- Root cause (working): likely node-level memory regression causing worker restarts; exacerbated by high fanout + large context lengths
- Mitigations applied: decreased fanout concurrency, pinned model variant, KV-cache reuse, nginx throttle for long-context, cordoned suspect node
- Customer impact: streaming sessions aborted for ~2% of total customers and up to 12% error rate on affected routes during peak; no data loss
- Next steps: collect cores, soak fixed node, RCA, rollback timeouts after 30m stable
```

carla (eng): I'll start an RFC for long-term controls: backpressure per-client, more aggressive prefix caching, and per-route memory caps.

tess (support): updating customers now with ETA and what to expect.

mike (infra): metrics trending back to normal. Will keep watch.

sara (SRE - oncall): closing live mitigation thread; handoff to kevin/mike/carla for postmortem. If anything spikes again, re-open and page. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin (runtime): leaving links to artifacts: logs: https://logs.redwood.io/4089990123, cores: s3://redwood-ops/incident-4089990123/coredumps, dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/streaming/incident-4089990123

tess (support): noted, will include links in customer emails.

incident-bot: Incident channel thread archived to incidents-archive/4089990123 for RCA prep.
_notes: This thread simulates a live incident coordination: paging, quick mitigations, config commands, customer comms, and handoff. Messages are ordered chronologically and include bot messages and code/log blocks per agents.md.
